title: Reefer Cargo Services: Request Lead Time and Late Requests
content:
Every Reefer Cargo Services tier expects an order a certain number of calendar days ahead of the vessel's scheduled departure. This page defines when an order counts as on time, what happens to one that arrives later, and how the late request fee attaches.

## Clause

The reference date is the scheduled departure date shown on the booking record. Counting back from it by the tier's lead time in calendar dates gives the last on-time date. An order received on that date or on any earlier date is on time. An order received after that date is late. A late order is taken only on a tier that accepts late orders, and it then carries the tier's late request fee, charged once for the service. On a tier that does not accept late orders, a late order is not taken. The departure date is read from the booking record at the time of the order; the customer's own statement of the sailing date does not replace it.

## Outcomes

| Order date against the last on-time date | Tier accepts late orders? | Result |
|---|---|---|
| on or before it | either | on time; no late request fee |
| after it | yes | taken, with the late request fee charged once |
| after it | no | not taken |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical dates and lead time)

Take an imaginary tier with a lead time of 5 calendar days.

- Scheduled departure 20 April 2026: the last on-time date is 15 April 2026. An order received on 15 April is on time; one received on 16 April is late.
- Scheduled departure 3 March 2026: counting back five calendar dates across the month end gives 26 February 2026. An order on 26 February is on time; one on 27 February is late.
- If that imaginary tier accepted late orders, the 16 April order would be taken with one late request fee; if it did not, the order would not be taken at all.

## Points of judgement

- Calendar dates are counted, so weekends and public holidays count like any other day, and the time of day at which the order arrives plays no part.
- The late request fee is a single charge for the service; it does not grow with the number of days by which the order is late.
